newsitem.title: UK: Russian seaborne fuel exports slump in Nov - Petra.
newsitem.headline: Russian seaborne fuel exports slump in Nov - Petra.

text.p: Seaborne fuel oil exports from the Black Sea ports of Novorossiisk, Tuapse and Odessa and the Baltic port of Ventspils dropped sharply in November, shipping inspectors Petrak said.
Fuel oil exports from the four ports totalled 551,721 tonnes in November compared with 674,723 tonnes in October.
Exports out of Novorossiisk were down from 268,000 tonnes to 196,000 tonnes, while Odessa shipped only 131,000 tonnes against 191,000 tonnes.
Shipments from Tuapse were actually 2,000 tonnes higher in November at 107,000 tonnes compared with October.
Russian exports from the Baltic port of Ventspils were also higher at 117,000 tonnes against 110,000 tonnes.
Data from the other main Baltic fuel oil export ports -- St Petersburg, Tallinn and Klaipeda -- was not provided.
Fuel oil traders said exports were not as low as first anticipated since no export tariff has been levied and Russian fuel continues to be marketed on strong international markets.
